It supports an o-shaped body but does not let the complete glyph or any earlier impression be read securely. The position is qualified instead of being silently supplied from the word.

E-n, d-apostrophe-autres, termes and the final comma are legible on a slightly rising line above the cancelled end of the clause, with En beginning to the left of trivial. The addition is interlinear, not in the margin or consecutive on the base line.
The old short serifed l remains under a larger looped handwritten L. They share one type position, and the new capital is followed by the typed a.
A typed serifed l is crossed or reworked by an oblique pen stroke extending below its base. An upper loop is not securely separated from the old upright, so C’s ell/l doubt is retained.

changes.place: cancelled extra glyph in first coéfficients

The character is a single typewritten curved C with two terminal serifs. No second vertical or doubled contour is drawn.
A typed curved right parenthesis lies immediately after C under crossing pen strokes; the following short hyphen remains live.
The upright curved parenthesis is crossed several times just before the live full stop. The mark is not part of the accent or final e.

changes.place: quoted second theorem, case and quotation signs
changes.shows: The second theorem word begins with a tall capital T and a long top crossbar. Two short strokes open the quoted phrase and two close it; no angular guillemets are present. Accent qualifications are recorded separately.

Above the first e, a faint rising left stroke meets a shorter dark descending right stroke, making a peaked mark. A small hooked acute cannot be excluded, so the circumflex-shaped reading is preferred but qualified.

Above the second e is a broad arch with both ends descending. Its rounded circumflex shape is clearer than a single grave stroke, but the faint left limb prevents certainty. The accent is not normalized from the word.

The enlarged and rotated name separates the initial L, e, crossed looped f, s curve, open c, tall h, e, t and terminal descending z. The crowding does not prevent the letters being read; C’s doubt is removed.

Beneath the new S there is a typewritten left upright, a broad lower bowl and a basal foot. These favour an older D, but the crossing S obscures enough of the outline that an old S remains possible. The underlying ink omitted by both witnesses is kept qualified.

The replacement a-i-t is typewritten immediately above the cancelled final e of constitue. A pen leader runs below ait, drops left to the old e and curves upward on the right; the base le remains below and to its right.
The x strikes leave e and n, then the t ascender/crossbar, rounded o and descending p separately visible. C’s doubt is resolved and H’s omission restored.

The first letter has a tall stem and upper P bowl, so the capital is secure. After the comma and l, the cancelled last vowel has a lower closed bowl and a right foot favouring a, but crossing strokes leave e possible; neither witness’s unqualified ending is adopted.
A small e loop/opening and a separate t with upper stem and cross-stroke remain beneath the pen strike. Both letters are readable; C’s doubt is removed.

changes.place: under handwritten capital C in Ce sont
changes.shows: The large handwritten C overlays a smaller typewritten curved body at the same baseline as e. The small form is consistent with c, but its opening is masked by the new C; its reading remains qualified.

changes.place: two overlapping type positions in arithmétiques
changes.shows: At each of the two positions after arithmét, a dotted i form coexists with a q bowl and descender. Both positions visibly contain both impressions. Their order of printing is not recoverable securely, so the paired overlays are preserved with qualified alternatives.

Every letter of the struck rédacteur remains legible. The handwritten r-a-p-p-o-r-t-e-u-r is directly above it, with both p descenders and the tall crossed t distinct after rotation. There is no marginal displacement.

The first type position contains an open c-shaped left curve and the upper/lower curves and central crossing of s. The forms are superposed; the image does not establish which impression was last. Both are represented at one position instead of choosing a whole word from syntax.

After the typed R, the first old vowel retains an e eye and lower curve beneath a smaller added i. The next old typewritten i retains its dot and serifs beneath a low handwritten e loop. The corrections are spatially distinct from the old ei and give ie; both layers are kept.

The second occurrence again shows a serifed typed l with an added diagonal pen stroke and a lower continuation. As in the first occurrence, no securely separate upper loop settles ell against reworked l; the same local uncertainty is marked at both places.

changes.place: end of cancelled restent valables sous une
changes.shows: After sous and a struck space, the typewritten u sides, n shoulder and final e eye remain visible through the x strikes. The cancelled une is present and readable.

changes.place: overprint at final vowel of tordus
changes.shows: The position after tord contains the ascender and bowl of d as well as the two uprights/cup of u. The preceding d is a separate normal typed letter. The two forms in the final vowel position overlap and their printing order is left uncertain.

The n-o-m-b-r-e-u-x forms are legible above the left part of ingrédients. A long curved leader below the word descends to the gap before ingrédients and curls upward over the middle of that typed word. Both the raised addition and the leader are retained.

The single pen strike crosses all of nécessaires while leaving its letters and acute readable. The replacement indispensables is written directly above, with i dots, d ascender, p descender and b/l rises distinguishable in the rotated enlargement.

changes.place: quotation signs around théorie des motifs
changes.shows: Two high short typewriter strokes occur at each end of the phrase. The o of motifs is a filled round type impression without separable earlier letter strokes; no additional letter is inferred.

changes.place: last word, handwritten replacement over old type
changes.shows: A long handwritten s precedes a clean typed e. The following dark position has an upper running hand stroke and a downstroke supporting r over an older two-curved s-like body; the last position has a looped handwritten a and rightward tail over a taller crossed t-like remnant. The r and both old letters remain qualified, while the visible s, e and final a are retained.

inspection_note: Root alone viewed the whole supplied scan and both actual supplied halves before C, the full H slice, all11 C doubts, all3 spelling-slip entries and all32 C inventory elements. Every agreed word and sign was checked against the ink line by line; both actual halves were reread after the detailed decisions. All74 recorded crops were actually viewed, including rotated title/interlinear additions/replacement words and the final overprint, all cancellations and margins, arrow/field/ell labels, accents, punctuation, underlines and every C doubt. Trivialite, en top, et and Lefschetz are resolved from the ink; opening U/u and Reimann/Riemann preserve both layers. Both witnesses flatten internal overprints and omit old letters beneath the large S/C and final replacement. The two ell/l forms, two arched accents, several old letters and printing orders remain qualified. The E-like initial mark may be graphical; its visible bent tail is drawn without asserting a word. The trailing H section Divers types de Q-ell-faisceaux introduces a different sheet and has no corresponding writing on this page; it is treated as a source-boundary heading, not an omitted manuscript passage or collation item. Handwritten elements are attributed only to another unnamed hand. Archive122 remains a comment. No mathematical claim has been checked, no ordered second audit is claimed, and context remains sealed.
